messages:
Marta: Quick design review — sharing the mock for the autoscale header. Main asks: 1) how do we surface a pool fallback hint when the selected GPU pool has no burst capacity, 2) VoiceOver/screen-reader flow for the SLO slider, and 3) keyboard/tab behavior when fallback happens. Can we focus on accessibility + copy + layout impact? Devin: I like the hint, but worried about layout shift. If hint appears inline below pool name it pushes the SLO slider down and Tab order moves — that feels jarring. Could we do an overlay or absolute-positioned callout instead? Kevin: Overlay avoids push but overlays can be dismissed by keyboard and might not be announced by screen readers. Another option: keep it inline visually but avoid DOM reflow so focus stays put. Also consider an always-present small hint icon (info) with aria-describedby on hover/focus. Samir: Accessibility thoughts: avoid focus jumps. Use an aria-live region (role="status") to announce a fallback when it happens, and keep focus on the pool picker control. Implementation sketch: ```
Burst unavailable — routing to fallback pool.
``` Make sure the message is included in DOM beforehand (hidden via offscreen CSS) so announcing doesn’t cause new focus. Also add aria-describedby to pool name so VoiceOver users can query context. aria-bot: Automated a11y scan results (quick): - Missing aria-label on SLO slider (role=slider needs aria-valuemin/max/now and aria-label). - Pool hint contrast ratio 3.8:1 (target >=4.5:1 for small text). - Dynamic content not announced on VoiceOver iOS in overlay mode. Marta: Great catches. Copy options: long: "Burst currently unavailable for this pool. Requests will be routed to fallback pool automatically." Short: "Burst unavailable — routing to fallback pool." Which should we use in the status region? Short is better for announcements. Also include a link in the hint to docs: "Learn more about pool fallbacks." Devin: Short copy + docs link sounds good. For keyboard flow: when a user tabs into pool picker and the UI switches to fallback, we must keep focus on the pool picker and expose the status message (aria-live) so screen readers hear it but the keyboard cursor doesn't move. Also ensure Esc doesn't dismiss the status. Kevin: Minor UI nit: if we use an info icon, its hit target must be >= 44px. Mobile voiceover users need a clear tap target. Also ensure the SLO slider has visible focus ring and we don't hide default focus for custom styled track. Samir: Will add the following checklist to the PR: - add aria-live role="status" element pre-mounted in DOM - populate with short announcement text on fallback event - add aria-describedby on pool element pointing to status id - add aria-label/aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax/aria-valuenow to SLO slider - increase hint text contrast and bump icon hit area to 44px - unit/integration tests that assert announcements triggered and focus preserved Marta: Can someone prototype both overlay and inline-no-reflow in Figma? I want to test perceived discoverability vs. announcement reliability. Also capture copy variants for user testing. Devin: I can mock overlay vs inline today. I'll also record a quick VoiceOver demo showing current failing behavior. Kevin: I'll audit CSS for layout shifts in the header and propose a container size that prevents reflow when the hint appears. Samir: I'll open a draft PR with the aria-live patch + slider ARIA props and add a note in the ticket about contrast. Marta: Awesome. Thanks team — syncing on this Friday to pick the approach for rollout. :thumbsup: Devin: +1 Kevin: 👍 aria-bot: Accessibility scan scheduled for PR #1234 after changes are pushed.
